html:
The Black Death reached Norway in 1349, carried by a ship from England to Bergen. Within about a year it had killed perhaps half of the population.

It spread along the coast and up the valleys. Farms were abandoned on a huge scale, and many stayed empty for centuries. With fewer people, the crown and the nobility lost much of their income, and most of the clergy died.

Historians link the plague to Norway's long decline in the late Middle Ages: it fell under the Kalmar Union and then under Danish rule in Denmark-Norway, and lost its own nobility. It was part of the Black Death that swept Europe. See Norway.
